title: American government and constitutional foundations
audience: a pre-law college student (any major) preparing for law school and the LSAT
purpose: Explain the Constitution's design, federalism, Congress, the presidency, the courts and judicial review, civil liberties and civil rights, elections, parties, interest groups and public policy.

weeks.12: Foreign policy and state and local government

blocks.deliverable: Map which level of government handles ten policy areas.
Summarize the holdings of five landmark rights cases.
Trace a bill through Congress and explain the veto and override.
Week 7 midterm; explain how a case reaches the Supreme Court.
Describe how one policy is made and carried out at three levels of government.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Policy brief: choose an issue handled by several branches and levels of government, and explain neutrally the constitutional authority, the institutions involved and the arguments on each side, in 1,500 words.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
